notes: A zero-finding pass, recorded so these ten items are never read for addresses again. The Western Addition Parcel Appraisal Reports, SFH371-5039 to SFH371-5048: the Redevelopment Agency's 1955 appraisals of the parcels it meant to buy in project area A-1, blocks 713, 720-723, 725, 727, 733-737, 754-756, 1078 and 1097-1099. Each typed sheet gives the parcel number, block and lot, the street address, a description of the building (storeys, construction, units, sometimes the year built and dated modernization), a rent schedule by room, and a photograph; the fuller reports add the deed history and the owner. Every page was OCR'd with Tesseract at 300 dpi (the Internet Archive text layer misses most sheets). The question that decides a batch like this is not what the sheets say but whether the building they describe still stands, so the pass was run resolution-first: the 2025 roll was asked for every parcel on these blocks with a building dated before 1956 (44 parcels), and every street number EAS gives those parcels was looked for in the OCR, by street and then by number alone. None is among the appraised properties: the Agency appraised what it was buying, and what it bought on these blocks was cleared for the Geary Expressway, the Japanese Cultural and Trade Center and the A-1 rebuilding. The survivors are the institutional and later buildings the Agency left in place, and the Golden Gate Avenue frontage of blocks 754-756, which these items do not reach. Nine passages mention a building moved within its lot or brought in from elsewhere before 1955; none names an address the house-moves captions or the property summaries connect to a standing building. Owners, grantors, grantees, tenants and appraisers are not transcribed.

coverage.remaining: Nothing in these ten items. In the same collection: the 50-building conservation study (SFH371-5000), the appraisal and comparable-sales volumes (5001 to 5038) and the Yerba Buena Phase 1 block files (5055 to 5078).
coverage.note: 10 items, 1,388 PDF pages: 172 sheets with an address header, about 100 that state a construction year or a building's age, 33 with a legible 'built in' year. 44 parcels on these blocks hold a building the 2025 roll dates before 1956; none of their street numbers appears as an appraised property. Zero findings.
